links.comparator_used: Clinician-authored replies composed independently, with AI drafts generated but never shown to physicians
links.outcome: Blinded physician ratings of message quality (effectiveness, misunderstanding potential, harm) and draft incorporation into final messages
links.effect: 2264 (11%) of displayed drafts were incorporated into final messages (BERTScore F1 = 0.93); independent physician messages were moderately similar to unseen drafts (BERTScore F1 = 0.83); physicians preferred human-authored messages (4.24/5)
links.tradeoff: Low uptake: only 11% of displayed drafts were incorporated into final messages. Automated semantic similarity did not capture the preference for human-authored messages.
links.quote: Despite comparable semantic scores, physicians preferred human-authored messages (4.24/5).

links.comparator_used: Blinded physician expert ratings of effectiveness, misunderstanding potential and harm
links.outcome: Correlation of automated metrics (BLEU, ROUGE, BERTScore, Flesch Reading Ease) with physician quality ratings
links.effect: BERTScore correlated with physician quality ratings in the intervention group but not in the non-displayed group; metrics assessed editing fidelity but failed to evaluate whether AI content matches independent human performance
links.tradeoff: Automated metrics are valid only in specific contexts and can give misleading assurance when drafts are compared with independent human writing.
links.quote: BERTScore correlated with physician quality ratings in the intervention group but not in the non-displayed.

design_hint: silent-mode deployment and automated metric validation against clinician review
